key_insight: The paper replaces Lagrange-multiplier enforcement of Dirichlet boundary velocities with a lifting-based kinematic decomposition that strongly imposes boundary motion while preserving a structure-preserving ODE formulation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate and computationally convenient way to model actuated elastodynamic systems in FEM, avoiding DAEs and improving boundary fidelity without sacrificing energy-consistent port-Hamiltonian structure.
method: Split displacement and velocity into a zero-boundary dynamic part plus a prescribed lifting field.
Embed the lifting as a distributed port in a port-Hamiltonian virtual power formulation.
Derive lifted 2-field and 4-field FEM models that remain ODEs and recover standard FEM under specific shape functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations showing the proposed method preserves energy-balance properties and improves computational performance, while also matching classic matrix-partitioning FEM in special cases.
watch_item: The quality of the method depends on choosing suitable lifting/shape functions, so implementation details may affect accuracy and equivalence to standard FEM.
paper_title: Strong imposition of Dirichlet boundary velocities in structure-preserving discretizations of elastodynamics
